newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed on Tuesday with many investors staying on the sidelines for a clearer direction after the London Metal Exchange (LME) closed the Monday kerb down, traders said.
Copper continued its short-term downtrend on the LME, losing grip of the $2,300 mark as stocks kept rising. Prices shed $27.50 to $2,282, with support pegged at $2,270 and $2,250.
In Shanghai, the key November 1997 contract ended at 21,100 yuan ($2,547) per tonne, rising 50 yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 20,880 and hit a high of 21,110 yuan per tonne.
August was unchanged at 20,700, September fell 60 to 20,850, October 50 to 21,000, December rose 80 to 21,130 and the January 1997 contract dropped 100 to 21,000 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 40,770 tonnes from 57,550 tonnes.
Traders said many investors were uncertain about short-term market trend and so covered their positions.
"Little speculative selling emerged after copper opened lower, and that prevented further losses," one trader said.
"But many investors offset their positions on mixed views over where the market is heading," he said.
In Shanghai, physical prices consolidated around 20,700 to 20,800 yuan due to a lack of end-user buying, traders said.
They said copper was likely to move in a narrow range in the short term, with investors waiting for fresh stimulus.

Aluminium ended mostly up. August rose 10 to 14,290 yuan per tonne, September, the only losing contract, fell 60 to 14,500, October rose 30 to 14,650, November 20 to 14,660 and December 310 to 14,720 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 7,240 tonnes from 4,130 tonnes.
